name: I2C Address Map
blurb: devices on a bus by address, with conflicts and alternative addresses
intro: Lists the devices of one I2C bus by 7-bit address, from a list of part names (with or without addresses) or a pasted i2cdetect grid. Parts it knows get their default address and the addresses their strap pins allow, so conflicts come with a free alternative or a mux suggestion; reserved addresses follow NXP UM10204.

inputs.label: Devices, one per line
inputs.default:
BME280
SSD1306 0x3C
MPU6050
DS3231
INA219 x3
AT24C32 0x57
MCP23017 0x20
my-sensor 0x29
inputs.help: Part name, optional address (0x48, 48h) and optional count (x3). Unknown parts need an address. Or paste the output of i2cdetect -y 1.

examples.title: Sensor board with a classic 0x68 clash (IMU and RTC)

usage: Give list as text, one device per line: a part name (BME280, INA219, SSD1306 …), an optional address (0x48 or 48h) and an optional count (x3); or paste an i2cdetect -y grid. format = 7bit or 8bit. Returns a table per device with its address, status (ok, CONFLICT, reserved, not allowed for the part), the free alternatives its pins allow and how to set them, plus warnings with a concrete fix, a bus map and C #defines. Use it when adding a device to an I2C bus or debugging a scan.
sources: NXP UM10204 I2C-bus specification rev. 7, section 3.1.12 and table 4 (reserved addresses)

Device datasheets for the default and strap addresses (Bosch BME280, Solomon SSD1306, TDK MPU-6050, Maxim DS3231, TI INA219/ADS1115/TMP102, Microchip MCP23017/24LC256, ST VL53L0X, NXP PCA9685, TI TCA9548A and others)
